note: One real instance of every problem code, produced by running the named function over a document that provokes it. The `message` strings are verbatim: the canvas renders them unaltered, so a client test asserting against a paraphrase would be asserting about a fiction.

instances.scenario: a tool dropped onto a gate instead of onto an agent
instances.why: An attach edge runs from a tool, an MCP server or a skill TO an agent or a crew, and only that way: it says what that agent HAS, so there is nothing for it to mean pointing anywhere else. This is the most likely wrong drop on a canvas where a gate sits between two agents.

problem.message: edge 'e4' attaches a tool node to a gate node. An attach edge runs from a tool, an MCP server or a skill TO an agent or a crew, and only that way: it says what that agent has, so there is nothing for it to mean in any other direction

instances.scenario: more attachment nodes than the document ceiling
instances.why: Counted SEPARATELY from MAX_GRAPH_NODES, because that bound's 24 comes from the 2,000-frame replay ring and an attachment emits no frames at all - applying the ring's arithmetic to a thing it was not about would be a number that happens to be right for the wrong reason.

problem.message: this graph has 25 tool, MCP and skill nodes and the ceiling is 24 (MAX_ATTACHMENT_NODES). Attachments are counted separately from steps - they never run and never bill - so this is a bound on the document rather than on what the run costs

instances.scenario: a tool node nobody attached to anything
instances.why: A WARNING and not an error, because it is exactly what a node looks like the moment it is dropped - refusing it would mean an author cannot put a tool on the canvas before deciding whose it is. It is also why an attachment is exempt from `node-unreachable`: that would be a second, louder row about the same omission.

problem.message: 'scraper' is a tool node attached to nothing, so nothing in this graph can use it. That is legal - it is what a node looks like the moment it is dropped - but a run would never reach it

instances.scenario: one agent holding more attachments than the per-node ceiling

problem.message: 'draft' holds 9 attachments and the ceiling is 8 (MAX_ATTACHMENTS_PER_NODE). What this bounds is the agent's system prompt rather than the run's price: every attachment contributes a tool schema or a skill preamble, and past some width an agent stops choosing between them well

instances.scenario: four loops against the cycle ceiling, one of them from a plain agent
instances.why: `back-edge-not-router` is the measured one: with a plain node closing the loop the join fires once, the second arrival is suppressed, and the run ends normally having produced nothing - no exception, no warning.

problem.message: edge 'e9' closes a loop from 'b' back to 'a', and 'b' is a agent node. A loop-closing node MUST be a router: insert a router node between 'b' and 'a' and draw the back edge from that router instead. This is measured, not cautious - with a plain node here the join fires once, the second arrival is suppressed, and the run ends normally having produced nothing, with no exception and no warning

instances.scenario: more model-calling nodes than the billable ceiling

problem.message: this graph has 14 nodes that call a model and the ceiling is 13 (MAX_BILLABLE_NODES), which is the shipped validator's 8 with the same 1.7 headroom MAX_GRAPH_NODES applies. This bound is about shape rather than spend - what a graph COSTS is checked separately, against the per-run ceiling, and that check names a dollar figure you can act on

instances.scenario: a graph whose worst case prices past the per-run ceiling

problem.message: this graph's worst case prices at $8.24 over 288 model calls, and $10.30 with the 1.25x margin, against a per-run ceiling of $10.00. Remove a node that calls a model, move one to the cheap tier, take a node off a cycle, or lower a retry ceiling

instances.scenario: a tier pointed at a model PRICES cannot price
instances.why: Provoked by pointing the cheap tier at a slug with no PRICES entry, which is the shape a model swap without a matching price commit takes. The failure it stands against is the one that reported a 128,069-token run at $0.00: `PRICES.get(model, (0.0, 0.0))` turning 'no price on file' into 'this call was free'.

problem.message: this graph cannot be priced: openrouter/example/unpriced-preview has no entry in PRICES, so every call it makes would contribute $0.00 to a total that is supposed to bound spend. Add the model to data/models.json in the same commit that names it

instances.scenario: an agent naming a credential that is not in the caller's vault
instances.why: Plan 01 D10: absent and foreign are ONE code, because the vault answers both with one exception and a canvas that could tell them apart would be an oracle for other people's ids. Only produced when the caller has an identity; this fixture validates as somebody whose vault is empty.

problem.message: draft names the credential cr_0badc0de, which is not in your vault; pick one of your own or create it first

instances.scenario: an authored crew with no members at all
instances.why: A crew with no members compiles to a Crew with no tasks and hands back nothing - the same silent-empty-result failure `back-edge-not-router` exists for, arrived at from the other direction.

problem.message: the authored crew 'team' has 0 member agents and a crew takes 1 to 6 (MAX_CREW_MEMBERS, the shipped validator's own six). With none it compiles to a Crew with no tasks and hands back nothing; the ceiling is the largest team this repository has ever run

instances.scenario: four loops against the cycle ceiling, one of them from a plain agent
instances.why: `back-edge-not-router` is the measured one: with a plain node closing the loop the join fires once, the second arrival is suppressed, and the run ends normally having produced nothing - no exception, no warning.

problem.message: this graph closes 4 loops and the ceiling is 3 (MAX_CYCLES), the validator's own measured back-edge count. Each loop multiplies the price of every node inside it

instances.scenario: a gate allowing more revise turns than the cycle-iteration ceiling

problem.message: gate 'confirm' allows 4 revise turns and the ceiling is 3 (MAX_CYCLE_ITERATIONS), because a revise loop is a cycle and every node on one is billed again each time round. It is deliberately below the validator's own 5: that number prices a human in the loop, who is both the cause of the delay and the brake on it, and a builder cycle need not have one

instances.scenario: two nodes and two edges sharing an id

problem.message: 2 edges share the id 'e1'; ids address a node in every frame, every edge and every problem message, so they must be unique

instances.scenario: two nodes and two edges sharing an id

problem.message: 2 nodes share the id 'step'; ids address a node in every frame, every edge and every problem message, so they must be unique

instances.scenario: an edge arriving at the input node

problem.message: edge 'e2' arrives at 'idea', and an input node starts the run and has nothing upstream of it

instances.scenario: an edge naming a node that was deleted

problem.message: edge 'e2' names 'ghost' as its target, and no node has that id

instances.scenario: an edge leaving an agent by a gate's port

problem.message: edge 'e2' leaves 'draft' by the port 'approve', and a agent node offers out

instances.scenario: more escalation-tier nodes than the escalation ceiling

problem.message: this graph puts 9 nodes on the escalation tier and the ceiling is 8 (MAX_ESCALATION_NODES), the validator's own measured split of 5 escalation to 3 cheap carried up by the same headroom as the node count. Move one to the cheap tier

instances.scenario: one node fanning out wider than the concurrency ceiling

problem.message: 'idea' fans out to 5 nodes and the ceiling is 4 (MAX_FANOUT_WIDTH), the validator's own measured maximum. What this bounds is concurrent branches, and the real constraint behind it is GitHub's 10 requests a minute per IP

instances.scenario: a router declaring the same branch label twice
instances.why: The two codes come from one mistake, and `ident-collision` comes from nothing else. Method idents are n<index>_<id> and event labels e<index>_<port>, and the index is unique per node, so the ONLY way two compiled names collide is a router emitting one label twice - which is what a duplicate branch is.

problem.message: 2 nodes compile to the same router label 'e1_same'; frames from both would attribute to one node

instances.scenario: a gate whose id leaves no room for its compiled router

problem.message: 'gaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa' compiles to the flow method 'n2_route_gaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa', which does not match ^n[0-9]{1,2}_[a-z0-9_]{1,40}$. A gate compiles to two methods and the second is prefixed 'route_', so a gate's id has six characters less room than any other node's; shorten it

instances.scenario: two input nodes asking for the same key

problem.message: 2 input nodes both ask for 'idea'; the run request carries one value under that name and there would be no saying which node it seeded

instances.scenario: an input node asking for a different key than the document declares

problem.message: the document declares input_field 'idea' and no input node asks for it; the input nodes ask for topic

instances.scenario: joins naming a node that is not there, and one with a single arrival

problem.message: 'step' is declared a join and 1 edge(s) arrive at it. A join over one edge is the same as no join at all

instances.scenario: joins naming a node that is not there, and one with a single arrival

problem.message: joins names 'ghost', and no node has that id

instances.scenario: an agent whose task placeholders are left unfilled

problem.message: draft runs 'scoper', whose task needs human_override, idea and this node does not supply them

instances.scenario: a crew that is registered but cannot be constructed
instances.why: `SynthesisCrew` takes typed findings at construction, so a document naming it once compiled, published and priced cleanly and then raised a bare TypeError at the first PAID run - after the scoper and all three research branches had billed.

problem.message: combine: the crew 'synthesis' cannot be built from a document: SynthesisCrew requires market, sentiment, feasibility at construction, and those are typed findings the validator flow hands over in Python rather than anything a drawn graph can supply. The crews a document may name are feasibility, market, scope, sentiment

instances.scenario: an agent naming a library id this deployment does not register

problem.message: draft names the agent 'nobody'; the registered agents are feasibility_analyst, market_analyst, reporter, scoper, sentiment_analyst, synthesist

instances.scenario: an MCP node that checks no tools
instances.why: An incomplete graph rather than an invalid document, so document.py allows it and bounds reports it - the difference between a problem in the dock and a save that fails.

problem.message: hands names a server and checks none of its tools; pick at least one, or the agent gains nothing from the attachment

instances.scenario: an MCP server that is not this caller's
instances.why: Absent and foreign are one answer, for the reason above.

problem.message: hands names the MCP server ms_ffffffffffff, which is not one of yours; add it in the MCP panel first

instances.scenario: an MCP tool whose description matches an injection pattern
instances.why: The fifth warning. PLANS.md decision 8: the tool stays selectable and the author decides, because the thirteen patterns have false positives by design - `act as` is ordinary English.

problem.message: hands checks 'search_docs', whose description matches 'ignore\\s+(previous|all|above|prior)\\s+instructions?'. That is often innocent - the pattern list has false positives - but the description reaches the agent's prompt, so read it before you ship

instances.scenario: an MCP tool the last discovery does not carry
instances.why: The shape a server RENAMING a tool takes. It is a validate problem rather than an exception because `tool_filter` simply fails to match and the agent runs without it.

problem.message: hands checks 'renamed' and 'Docs server''s last discovery does not carry it; re-discover the server

instances.scenario: a stored MCP server whose transport is no longer permitted
instances.why: The shape a document takes after MCP_STDIO_ENABLED is turned back off, which is why the transport is checked at validate and not only at create.

problem.message: hands uses 'Local server', and this deployment connects to remote MCP servers only; a stdio server would be a process started on the server by a document, and that is off by default

instances.scenario: an agent that is both a crew member and a step of the flow
instances.why: It cannot be both. As a member it runs inside its crew in the crew's own order, and as a step it runs again on its own - so nothing downstream could say which of the two outputs it was reading, and the author would be billed for both.

problem.message: 'worker' is a member of a crew and also carries 1 flow edge(s). It cannot be both: as a member it runs inside its crew, in the crew's own order, and as a step it runs again on its own - so nothing downstream could say which of the two outputs it was reading. Remove the flow edges, or the member edge

instances.scenario: an agent made a member of a transform
instances.why: Membership runs from an agent TO a crew. A crew is a team of agents and nothing else can be one of them, so the pair is checked rather than only the port - the port alone would let an author draw a transform into a crew and find out at the first paid run.

problem.message: edge 'e3' makes a agent node a member of a transform node. Membership runs from an agent TO a crew: a crew is a team of agents, and nothing else can be one of them

instances.scenario: JSON mode asked of a model that has none
instances.why: Every roster row supports JSON mode as measured on 2026-09-04, so this is provoked by patching one row's flag off rather than by finding a model that lacks it. The behaviour it stands against is the one the gauntlet names as the worst competitor habit: a parameter rendered, accepted, sent and silently dropped. Enforced twice - the inspector disables the control, and this fires anyway, so a stale client cannot smuggle it past.

problem.message: openai/gpt-4o-mini does not support JSON mode, so llm.response_format would be sent and dropped and this node would answer prose where the graph expects an object. Pick a model with JSON mode, or ask for text

instances.scenario: a registry row whose price crossed the ceiling after publish
instances.why: Unreachable against the live registry, and that is the point: config.py REFUSES an over-ceiling row at import, so this code can only fire on data that was legal when it was written and is not now. The scenario patches one roster row to $1.50 to reproduce a catalogue price moving under a published document. The repair is a refresh_models.py run, not an edit to the graph, which is why the message says so.

problem.message: openai/gpt-4o-mini is priced at $1.5000 per million input tokens, over the $1.00 ceiling. Its price moved after this graph was saved; pick a cheaper model

instances.scenario: an authored agent naming a model this build does not offer
instances.why: openai/o4-mini is the worked example of a model the registry refuses: exactly ONE endpoint, at $1.10 per million input, measured 2026-09-04. Under provider.max_price every candidate endpoint is filtered and the request fails rather than overspending, so the model is not merely dear - it is unservable. It is therefore absent from the roster, and a document naming it gets this code rather than model-over-ceiling.

problem.message: 'openai/o4-mini' is not a model this build offers, so llm.model names something no run could resolve. Pick one from the model picker; the roster is at GET /api/builder/models

instances.scenario: a graph with nothing to seed it

problem.message: this graph has no input node, so there is nothing to seed a run with and no field for the run request to carry

instances.scenario: an input node asking for a different key than the document declares

problem.message: this graph has no output node, so a completed run hands back no body. Everything it produced would be visible only as streamed frames

instances.scenario: more nodes than the graph ceiling

problem.message: this graph has 26 nodes and the ceiling is 24 (MAX_GRAPH_NODES); above that a single pass of the graph no longer fits comfortably in the 2,000-frame replay ring, and a reconnecting client would receive an incomplete run with nothing saying so

instances.scenario: a node nothing leads to

problem.message: nothing leads to 'stranded' from an input node, so it can never run. Connect it, or delete it

instances.scenario: a router with five branches and no otherwise

problem.message: router 'wide' declares 5 branches; a router takes 2 to 4. Fewer than 2 is a decision that cannot go either way, and more than 4 crosses MAX_FANOUT_WIDTH

instances.scenario: a router with five branches and no otherwise

problem.message: router 'wide' declares the branch 'five' and no edge leaves by it, so a run taking that branch stops here. That is legal - it is how a graph ends early - but it is rarely intended

instances.scenario: a router declaring the same branch label twice
instances.why: The two codes come from one mistake, and `ident-collision` comes from nothing else. Method idents are n<index>_<id> and event labels e<index>_<port>, and the index is unique per node, so the ONLY way two compiled names collide is a router emitting one label twice - which is what a duplicate branch is.

problem.message: router 'pick' declares the branch 'same' 2 times; a branch label is the port an edge leaves by, so a duplicate makes the drawn edge ambiguous

instances.scenario: a router with five branches and no otherwise

problem.message: router 'wide' declares 0 otherwise branches and must declare exactly one. Without it a value that matches no comparison wedges the run at this router; with two, which one takes an unmatched value is a coin toss written into the document

instances.scenario: a skill pack that is not this caller's
instances.why: One code for absent, deleted and foreign. A built-in is checked without an identity and validates clean for everyone, which is why this cannot simply be reject anything you do not own.

problem.message: hands names the skill sk_ffffffffffff, which is not one of yours and is not a built-in; it may have been deleted

instances.scenario: a tool that needs a key with none named
instances.why: A DIFFERENT repair from `credential-missing` - add a key of this kind, rather than that id is not yours - and therefore a different code, which is the rule compiler.py already states for its library codes.

problem.message: hands runs 'Search the web (Firecrawl)', which needs a firecrawl key, and names none; add a firecrawl credential and pick it here

instances.scenario: a tool parameter the catalogue entry refuses
instances.why: The gauntlet forbids a parameter rendered in the UI that the compiler ignores; this is the same rule from the other side - a parameter the server refuses has to be reported rather than silently dropped.

problem.message: hands: 'provider' is one of serper, tavily, exa, brave; not 'nope'

instances.scenario: a tool this deployment does not have
instances.why: One code for a made-up id and for somebody else's custom tool, the rule `credential-missing` already states: a canvas that told the two apart would be an oracle for other people's ids.

problem.message: hands names the tool 'no_such_tool', which is not in this deployment's catalogue and is not one of yours; the builtins are research_market_landscape, analyze_community_sentiment, assess_technical_feasibility, firecrawl_scrape, firecrawl_crawl, firecrawl_search, web_search, http_request, scrape_website, postgres_query
